SPARETECH raises $20M Series B to help manufacturers cut industrial spare parts inventory by 60%
SPARETECH aims to cut manufacturers' spare parts inventory by 60% within three years with AI that ensures parts are available when they are needed

/PRNewswire/ -- SPARETECH, a provider of enterprise AI for spare parts management, today announced it has raised $20 million in Series B funding to help manufacturers cut their spare parts inventory without risking downtime. Blume Equity and Insight Partners co-led the round, with participation from Headline.

"Every customer we work with wants the same thing: the production line running with less inventory on the shelf. That is the problem we are going to solve with Maintenance teams, and our goal is to cut spare parts inventory by 60% in the next three years, while securing the same uptime."

"Every part sitting idle is cash that could be working somewhere else. We are building AI that makes sure the right part is available when a plant needs it and put those idle parts back into circulation, so the money tied up on the shelf can go back to growing the business."

Industrial automation keeps expanding, and a single new production line can add thousands of spare parts that someone has to stock. The problem grows with every machine that is installed. With the cost of capital rising, manufacturers can no longer afford to keep that much money sitting on the shelf. At the same time, AI can now secure availability at a scale no team could manage by hand.

"Often building resilience in supply chain ends up in building more inventories for spare parts. A much more suitable way would be a system, which secures better resilience with up to 60% less inventories sitting on the shelves. SPARETECH is exactly doing this. A fascinating opportunity especially for the manufacturing industry."

"SPARETECH is exactly the kind of business we back. Idle spare parts are a large, overlooked pool of wasted resources, and putting them back to work gives manufacturers a measurable return and the planet less waste. We are delighted to partner with Martin, Lukas, and the team as they scale."

SPARETECH will use the funding to continue building the AI that secures spare part availability for industrial companies and put their surplus parts back into circulation, expand its presence in North America and new regions, and deepen its work with existing customers.

"The next stage of SPARETECH's growth runs through North America. American manufacturers operate large plant networks with a lot of capital tied up in spare parts, and they need a partner built for that scale. Insight has spent decades helping software companies grow in the United States, and we are excited to support Martin, Lukas, and the team as they scale."

"The digital world is moving into the physical one, and Germany has the industrial substance to lead that shift. SPARETECH is building industrial AI for spare parts management, and it already gives maintenance and procurement teams confidence in uncertain times. This is where industrial AI starts to pay off for global manufacturers."
Trusted by manufacturers like Nestlé, Porsche, VW, Bosch, and Sanofi, the company is moving toward its vision of a zero-waste industrial sharing economy.
